nodes.summary: For every set $p$ of symbols, the complement of the ω-language of infinite words with infinitely many letters in $p$ is the ω-language of infinite words whose letters are eventually all in the complement of $p$.
nodes.title: Complement of “infinitely often”

nodes.summary: For a set $p$ of symbols, this is the nondeterministic Büchi automaton over the alphabet of symbols with states $\mathsf{false}$ and $\mathsf{true}$, single start state $\mathsf{false}$ and single accepting state $\mathsf{true}$. From $\mathsf{false}$ it may read any letter and move to either state; from $\mathsf{true}$ it may read only letters in $p$, and then it stays in $\mathsf{true}$.
nodes.title: Two-state Büchi automaton for “eventually always”

nodes.summary: For a set $p$ of symbols, the ω-language “eventually always $p$” consists of the infinite words $x_0 x_1 x_2 \ldots$ for which there is an $N$ with $x_k \in p$ for all $k \ge N$.
nodes.title: Eventually always

nodes.summary: For a set $p$ of symbols, this is the nondeterministic Büchi automaton over the alphabet of symbols with states $\mathsf{true}$ and $\mathsf{false}$, single start state $\mathsf{true}$ and single accepting state $\mathsf{true}$, in which reading a letter $x$ from either state leads to exactly one state: $\mathsf{true}$ if $x \in p$ and $\mathsf{false}$ otherwise. So the state records whether the last letter read…
nodes.title: Two-state Büchi automaton for “infinitely often”

nodes.summary: For a set $p$ of symbols, the ω-language “infinitely often $p$” consists of the infinite words $x_0 x_1 x_2 \ldots$ with $x_k \in p$ for infinitely many $k$.
nodes.title: Infinitely often

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
